title: V6 misfire under high load
summary: Toyota documents a high-load/high-speed misfire condition with an ECM calibration response.
action: Have a Toyota technician match the recorded conditions and current calibration. Do not recreate the high-load condition yourself.
limitations: Camry: WMI 4T1 / VDS BZ1HK; Avalon: WMI 4T1 / VDS BZ1FB. Camry hardware/software confirmation is required. Other engines and years are outside this bulletin.

title: 2.7L EcoBoost misfire and lean-code branches
summary: Ford describes separate calibration and injector leak-down branches; a code alone does not identify a failed injector.
action: Record all codes and the build date for Ford diagnosis. For a flashing running-engine warning, avoid hard acceleration/deceleration and obtain immediate service.
limitations: The injector/lean/misfire branch requires production before July 12, 2018 plus diagnostic confirmation. Software work depends on companion codes. Internal fuel-system testing is professional.

title: Paired lean codes and calibration
summary: GM describes paired lean codes with a possible software cause.
action: Ask service to check intake/oil-system connections and ECM calibration before further diagnosis.
limitations: Both codes are part of the documented condition. This is not an automatic sensor or injector replacement.

title: Paired lean codes and calibration
summary: GM describes paired lean codes with a possible software cause.
action: Ask service to check intake/oil-system connections and ECM calibration before further diagnosis.
limitations: Both codes are part of the documented condition. This is not an automatic sensor or injector replacement.

title: Catalyst codes with air-filter sealing concerns
summary: Debris bypassing an improperly sealed airbox can affect exhaust components.
action: Have service validate airbox sealing before replacing parts.
limitations: Only the listed engine RPOs and model years are covered; the code does not prove catalyst failure.

title: Catalyst codes with air-filter sealing concerns
summary: Debris bypassing an improperly sealed airbox can affect exhaust components.
action: Have service validate airbox sealing before replacing parts.
limitations: Only the listed engine RPOs and model years are covered; the code does not prove catalyst failure.

title: Misfire/rich codes after prerequisite updates
summary: Honda distinguishes a recurring-code repair branch from an engine-noise branch after applicable earlier updates.
action: Have Honda check VIN eligibility and completion of 18-114, 18-124 or 19-025 before applying 19-037.
limitations: EX, EX-L, Touring only; iN VIN eligibility required. Historical warranty-extension text does not establish coverage today.

title: P0430 and software interpretation
summary: Acura describes software interpreting sensor data as catalyst deterioration.
action: Have Acura confirm applicability, PGM-FI calibration and required transmission software.
limitations: 2017 MDX VIN limits: 2WD: 5FRYD3...HB000001–HB014264/5J8YD3...HL000001–HL000229; SH-AWD: 5FRYD4...HB000001–HB040999/5J8YD4...HL000001–HL000507. 2018 TLX: 2WD: 19UUB2...JA000001–JA003458; SH-AWD: 19UUB3...JA000001–JA001898. Confirm the complete VIN and current bulletin.
engine: TLX: V6; MDX excludes Sport Hybrid

title: P0430 with a qualified sensor-test result
summary: Lexus requires specified bank2 downstream oxygen-sensor readings before the bulletin repair applies.
action: Ask a Lexus technician to perform the documented tests; otherwise normal diagnosis applies.
limitations: The replacement bulletin covers 2010 only. Do not import 2011 applicability from its superseded predecessor or replace a catalyst from the code alone.

title: EVAP leak codes and fuel-cap verification
years: 2012 and newer in the March 2021 bulletin
summary: Nissan identifies a loose cap as one possible trigger and separates it from an actual EVAP leak.
action: For a loose-cap warning, stop safely and check cap installation using the exact owner manual. Persistent codes need professional diagnosis.
limitations: Excludes LEAF and Titan XD V8 diesel. Do not extend this historical scope to later capless designs without confirmation. No automatic cap or EVAP-part replacement.

title: TDI EGR-flow and soot-restriction checks
summary: Volkswagen documents an EGR-flow case requiring EGR/DPF inspection and charge-air leak checks.
action: Have a qualified diesel technician follow the matched bulletin and current diagnostic guidance.
limitations: This diesel-specific evidence does not apply to gasoline Golf/Jetta models. It does not authorize emissions-system removal.

title: Qualified catalyst repair requires matching software
summary: Volkswagen requires the qualified catalyst hardware repair and ECM update together.
action: Have service verify VIN and campaign/update history before applying the bulletin.
limitations: VIN pattern CA_JC000001–CA_JC999999. The revision removed 2019 vehicles because of campaign action; this is not 2019 coverage.

title: N63 native DME faults and injector diagnosis
summary: BMW documents injector-related starting, mixture and misfire symptoms only when ISTA testing confirms that branch.
action: Provide the complete native codes and VIN to BMW service.
limitations: US-specification/VIN restrictions apply. This is a limited-extension document, not a recall or current coverage promise. Native codes are not mapped to generic P-codes here.

title: Timing/correlation codes after engine replacement
years: AM 2010–2013; PS 2014–2019; SK3 2020-onward as documented May 2022
summary: An incorrectly positioned camshaft reluctor can trigger these codes following engine replacement.
action: Tell the repairer whether the codes first appeared after replacement; internal timing checks belong to a technician.
limitations: The codes must have been absent beforehand. Later-year coverage requires current KGIS confirmation; this is not every Soul timing fault.
engine: 2010–11: Beta 2.0L/Gamma 1.6L; 2012–13: Gamma 1.6L GDI/Nu 2.0L GDI; 2014–19: Gamma 1.6L GDI/Nu 2.0L GDI; SK3: Nu 2.0L MPI

title: P0128 campaign diagnostic-logic update
summary: Campaign T3T addresses a scoped ECM diagnostic-logic condition.
action: Ask Hyundai to check the VIN for an open campaign and the applicable software.
limitations: Only certain vehicles qualify. The bulletin’s no-drivability-symptom statement must not be generalized to overheating or unrelated P 0128 cases.

title: P012800 and guided thermostat diagnosis
years: Model years not specified by this engine-scoped source
summary: Mercedes describes slow coolant warm-up and requires software checking plus guided thermostat-heating-element diagnosis.
action: Have Mercedes service verify engine, VIN and current XENTRY instructions.
limitations: The source supplies no exact model/year applicability list. Replacement is conditional; this record must not be attached to every Mercedes model.

title: Scoped PCM diagnostic update
summary: Jeep lists these codes among conditions addressed by a PCM update.
action: Have service diagnose other faults first and verify both PCM and TCM software.
limitations: Engine, build date and market limits apply. The bulletin is not a universal thermostat or EVAP-parts replacement.

title: EVAP codes with a software branch
summary: Dodge associates this scoped EVAP-code condition with PCM software.
action: Ask service to verify related systems and other faults before reprogramming.
limitations: No support here for other engines or years. The update is professional work, not an owner reset procedure.
engine: 5.7L V8 Hemi MDS VVT EZH; LA

title: P0128 in a scoped eTorque software update
summary: P 0128 is among this PCM-update bulletin’s conditions.
action: Have service confirm the fault and current PCM, HCP and TCM software.
limitations: Build and engine restrictions are essential. The code alone does not establish thermostat failure.

title: Cummins diagnostic software update
summary: These are selected codes from the scoped ECM/PCM update; unrelated faults require diagnosis first.
action: Ask Ram service to verify VIN applicability, calibration and the transmission-specific completion procedure.
limitations: RSU 16-041 eligibility is VIN-based. This is not an emissions-delete instruction or a general repair for every diesel Ram.
engine: 6.7L I6 Cummins Turbo Diesel ETK; DJ/D2

title: Static P029900
summary: CAEB wastegate evaluation.
action: Follow current Audi guided diagnosis.
limitations: Requires matching vehicle and fault conditions.

title: Crankcase ventilation with lean or intake-leak codes
summary: Audi describes these ECM codes alongside possible crankcase-pressure faults, noises or oil leakage. Existing valve and pipe versions affect diagnosis.
action: Have the workshop confirm VIN applicability, the applicable 17D9 update and installed hardware before following the diagnostic branch.
limitations: A4: 2005 VIN 405683–999999; 2006–2007 000001–999999; 2008 000001–170087. A3: 2006 VIN 000150–999999; 2007 000001–999999; 2008 000001–151827. These are the bulletin’s displayed VIN ranges, not complete VINs; full vehicle identification and engine confirmation remain necessary.

title: 4.0 TFSI breather noise with intake or idle codes
summary: Audi describes warm-idle noise, intermittent warning lamps and these ECM codes. Breather leakage is a possible cause, not a diagnosis from the code alone.
action: Have a qualified technician match the documented noise and crankcase behavior before choosing a repair.
limitations: This record covers the bulletin’s A8 application with 4.0 TFSI; all VINs are listed within that scope. Other engines and years are outside this record. Both prescribed diagnostic checks must support the replacement branch.

title: Macan P0299
summary: Documented diagnostic branches.
action: Read the case guide.
limitations: 2015 Turbo only.

title: Cayenne and Panamera EVAP evidence request
summary: Porsche requested vehicles with these EVAP faults for investigation. The document establishes a scoped code association, not a confirmed cause or a prescribed component replacement.
action: Keep the complete fault display, vehicle details and symptoms for a Porsche service provider to evaluate against current vehicle-specific instructions.
limitations: Cayenne types 9YA/9YB and Panamera type 971 only. Fault combinations and sub-fault details can differ with engine and DME software. This historical analysis request is not a recall, universal fix or current warranty promise.

title: Early Cayenne and Panamera camshaft fault context
summary: Porsche lists several fault families that can accompany a camshaft-adjuster problem. Those codes alone do not establish that mechanical failure has occurred.
action: Keep the complete scan log for a Porsche technician. Internal timing checks and any repair decision need the manufacturer’s diagnostic procedure.
limitations: Only the listed early 92A and 970 variants and years are covered. The source additionally lists the P0340–P0349 sensor-code range. Do not infer applicability to other Cayenne or Panamera generations, or attempt internal engine inspection from this reference.
